original_question: For a statistical manifold, can one identify and study those for which the tension field of the identity map is parallel, where the paper notes that for the identity map one has tau(id) = tr_g K with K = nabla - nabla^g?
target_in_paper: Section 1 (Jun-ichi INOGUCHI, communicated by Hiroshi MATSUZOE), item 5, first bullet: “Investigate statistical manifolds with parallel τ(id).” The immediately preceding context recalls the harmonic-map setup and states that, for the identity map of a statistical manifold, the tension field is τ(id)=tr_g K, where K is the difference tensor. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06989))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact local target: the first bullet of Section 1, item 5. It keeps the focus on a statistical manifold, the identity map, the formula τ(id)=tr_g K with K=∇−∇^g, and the condition that this vector field be parallel. It also does not drift into the adjacent but different bienergy problem stated in the second bullet. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06989))
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation is the short open problem “Investigate statistical manifolds with parallel τ(id),” so the refined version should stay at exactly that scope rather than broadening to unrelated structure theory. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06989))

The nearby setup should be made explicit: item 5 first discusses harmonic maps from a statistical manifold to an affine manifold, and then says that a statistically harmonic self-map is a harmonic map from (M,∇) to (M,∇*), where ∇* is the conjugate connection with respect to g. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06989))

To be stand-alone, the notation ∇^g should be named as the Levi-Civita connection of g, and K should be identified as the difference tensor K=∇−∇^g, since this is the notation used in the motivating sentence immediately before the bullet. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06989))

The paper also gives the motivating interpretation that τ(id)=0 is exactly the apolarity condition, i.e. the statistical harmonicity of the identity map; this explains why the nonzero-but-parallel case is the next natural question. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06989))

The phrase “parallel” is left implicit in the paper; a fully stand-alone formulation should either specify the connection on TM with respect to which parallelism is meant or explicitly note that this choice must be fixed. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06989))

There are no extra hypotheses here to add: the paper does not impose compactness, curvature, dimension, homogeneity/degree, nilpotency, characteristic, or asymptotic qualifiers for this problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06989))
refined_question: Let (M,g,∇) be a statistical manifold, let ∇^g denote the Levi-Civita connection of g, and set K:=∇−∇^g. Since the tension field of the identity map satisfies τ(id_M)=tr_g K, investigate the statistical manifolds for which the vector field τ(id_M) is parallel. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06989))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, investigate statistical manifolds for which the trace vector field tr_g K of the difference tensor K=∇−∇^g is parallel. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06989))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the first bullet in Section 1, item 5, because the paper motivates that bullet by recalling the harmonic-map framework, identifying the identity-map tension field with tr_g K, and then immediately asking to investigate statistical manifolds with parallel τ(id). That makes the closest paper-faithful sharpening a minimal rewrite of that exact bullet with the notation spelled out, rather than a broader classification or a shift to the neighboring bienergy question. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06989))
